messages.author: 0839befa8a8b7d53
messages.subject: Gamma_ccdf compile error in 2.3.0, but only when using ~, not when using increment_log_prob
parts:
I reinstalled Rstan this morning and discovered that 2.3.0 has been released. So I immediately tried out some code that had been giving me problems in 2.2.0.

I'm happy to report you've fixed a bug with gamma_ccdf_log that was plaguing me. Thanks a *ton* for that. It was the last piece I needed to work for a big hidden Markov model.

However, there's a lingering curious bug. The model only compiles when I use gamma_ccdf_log in this way:

    increment_log_prob( gamma_ccdf_log( y[i] , alpha , beta ) );

But it fails to compile when I use it this way:

    y[i] ~ gamma_ccdf( alpha , beta );

Here's a taste of the massive compiler error that is spit out:

Error in compileCode(f, code, language = language, verbose = verbose) : 
  Compilation ERROR, function(s)/method(s) not created! file70ad64e494e5.cpp:176:32: error: no matching function for call to 'gamma_ccdf_log'
                lp_accum__.add(gamma_ccdf_log<propto__>(get_base1(y,i,"y",1), alpha, beta));

I'm attaching an R script that I used to isolate the issue and validate the model. Hopefully it's useful in debugging. 

I am using clang-503.0.40. Pasting my sessionInfo() below as well.

messages.author: 3f22b207863d2049
messages.subject: Re: Gamma_ccdf compile error in 2.3.0, but only when using ~, not when using increment_log_prob
parts:
In version 2.2.0, there are online gamma-related sampling statements "gamma" and "inv_gamma". I'm guessing it's the same in 2.3.0.

It seems you are trying to use the complementary cumulative distribution function for the gamma distribution as a probability density function. I.e., "gamma_ccdf" is not a sampling statement, and btw, doesn't exist as a function either in stan 2.2.0. However, there are related functions "gamma_ccdf_log" and "gamma_cdf" and "gamma_cdf_log".

parts:
Luc: 

You haven't understood me.

A compile error with the statement that the function 'gamma_ccdf_log' doesn't exist is not the intended behavior, because that function does exist, both in 2.2.0 and 2.3.0.

If some functions that end in _log can't be used with ~ notation, then maybe there's a more graceful way to handle that than to generate a mysterious error message.

On Wednesday, June 25, 2014 1:55:39 PM UTC-7, Luc Coffeng wrote:

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Gamma_ccdf compile error in 2.3.0, but only when using ~, not when using increment_log_prob
parts:
gamma_ccdf() is a complementary cumulative distribution so
it wasn't intended be used with sampling notation (~) as a density.
What should happen is the parser should throw an error saying you
can't use gamma_ccdf as a density.

The reason you're getting what you're getting is that
the suffix "_log" is what we use to mark densities. In retrospect,
that was a very bad decision --- we'll probably fix it in the near
future, but it's a lot of code renaming. Here's the issue to
track the fix:

https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/issues/711

- Bob

P.S. We've been waiting for PyStan for the 2.3 announcement.
